PullRequest.Title: Implement tabbed model picker collapse animation
PullRequest.Body: Collapses model picker when using auto

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The diff establishes the 200 ms trigger, `dom.animate` is a recursive requestAnimationFrame loop, and the traced context-view implementation performs synchronous geometry reads after writes. Exact milliseconds vary by hardware and DOM size, so severity is medium, but the repeated forced-layout mechanism and critical-path reachability are direct.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread DOM style, layout, and geometry computation for the context view and popup subtree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each Auto on/off transition schedules one callback per display frame for the full 200 ms animation (about 12 callbacks at 60 Hz, more on high-refresh displays); each callback forces geometry work, whose cost grows with the rendered popup/workbench DOM.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated synchronous layout on the animation critical path can consume the frame budget and make the new collapse/expand transition visibly stutter.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, toggling Auto refreshed the list in place but did not start a body-height animation or repeatedly invoke context-view layout per frame.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new collapse animation starts an unbounded requestAnimationFrame loop for its lifetime and calls IContextViewService.layout on every frame to keep the shrinking popup reanchored.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 456 installs `dom.animate(..., () => this._contextViewService.layout())` only for the newly introduced body-collapse animation; no equivalent per-frame relayout existed before the PR.
Findings.Title: Avoid full context-view layout on every animation frame
Findings.Impact: When a user toggles Auto in the tabbed model picker, the 200 ms transition repeatedly forces context-view layout while height is changing, causing animation jank on slower machines or complex workbench DOMs.
Findings.Evidence: The added dom.animate callback invokes _contextViewService.layout() every frame until the Web Animation finishes. ContextView.layout() reaches doLayout(), which writes top/left to 0, reads getDomNodePagePosition(view), getTotalWidth(view), and getTotalHeight(view), then writes top/left again. Those synchronous geometry reads follow style and animated-height writes, forcing layout during every animation frame. The added tests explicitly assert that layoutCount increases while the animation is in progress, confirming this is intentional repeated work rather than a one-time final relayout.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep anchoring with a compositor-friendly transform or interpolate the known anchor offset during the animation, and run the full context-view layout only at the end (and on interruption), rather than calling ContextView.doLayout on every frame.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the tabbed model picker while Auto is already selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click synchronously builds destinations, model items, the ActionList DOM, sizing data, and footer before ContextView can render the popup; the new collapse state is then applied immediately with no animation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available providers and models; sizing and active-tab item construction scale with those in-memory collections, while the visible list remains virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the UI thread; no async worker or limiter participates in opening.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The picker rebuilds list descriptors on each show from already-loaded model-service state; no new cache or cache miss behavior is introduced. The hidden list construction is the same work the pre-diff visible Auto picker already performed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: show() and ActionList construction are synchronous and directly traced, and initial collapse passes no fromHeight so it does not start the new frame loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large third-party model catalogs increase synchronous construction cost, but the diff does not add that construction or increase its cardinality, so it is not reportable here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-introduced performance regression: initial collapse adds small DOM/state work but the potentially scaling list build was already required and executed before the change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle Auto on or off while the model picker remains open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The switch synchronously selects the model, refreshes the existing ActionList, and starts the 200 ms collapse/expand animation. Every animation frame calls ContextView.layout before the transition can paint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue the existing chat.modelChange telemetry event from the selection callback
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Auto toggling already invoked the same onSelect callback and telemetry emission before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The enqueue call is synchronous but transport is not awaited; it is not the animation bottleneck.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One transition per user toggle; approximately duration divided by frame interval (about 12 callbacks at 60 Hz, more at higher refresh rates), with each layout covering the popup/context-view DOM.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one body animation/rAF loop per popup. Reversal clears and cancels the previous loop before starting another; there is no parallel burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing ActionList instance is reused and item descriptors are rebuilt from in-memory model state. No remote cache is consulted and no request is coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: dom.animate is a recursive requestAnimationFrame loop, and ContextView.doLayout performs style writes followed by synchronous geometry reads on every callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual forced-layout duration depends on hardware, workbench DOM complexity, and refresh rate; the per-frame geometry work and its placement on the animation path are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium rendering regression: the diff newly forces full context-view layout throughout each transition, risking dropped frames.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interrupt, hide, or enable reduced motion during a collapse/expand transition
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Disposal or reduced-motion notification clears the active animation store, cancels the Web Animation/rAF loop, performs one final context-view layout, and restores hover state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active animation and one cleanup sequence per popup; repeated reversals remain bounded because MutableDisposable clears the prior store.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI thread with a single owned animation; cancellation prevents overlapping frame loops.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership is in renderDisposables/bodyAnimation and tests cover hide, reversal, and reduced-motion completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Final-layout cost varies with DOM complexity, but it occurs once per interruption rather than growing over popup lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle regression; animation resources are bounded and canceled on replacement, hide, reduced motion, and disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh another TabbedActionListWidget consumer such as the session workspace picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A provider/session update rebuilds in-memory list items and now reads body.offsetHeight before updating the list. The new collapse callback is absent for these consumers, so no body animation or per-frame context layout starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing dev-container availability resolution that precedes a coalesced visible-picker refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most four checks concurrently; resulting UI refreshes are coalesced to at most one per 50 ms window
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same checks, limiter, cache, and refresh calls existed before the diff; only a single generic body-height read is added to each refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The checks are asynchronous; only the subsequent visible-list refresh is on the UI critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One refresh per provider event; dev-container availability refreshes are coalesced by a 50 ms scheduler after checks and availability work is bounded by a limiter of four.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Availability checks remain limited to four and visible-list refreshes are coalesced; the generic widget refresh itself is synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session workspace availability uses the existing map of booleans/promises, so warm entries avoid repeated checks; this PR does not alter keys, invalidation, or negative caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added read and caller frequency; low that it independently creates material user-visible cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: An offsetHeight read can flush pending style work, but this path reads before its list mutation and no realistic repeated forced-layout mechanism was established beyond one read per coalesced refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the unconditional height read should ideally be gated to collapsible consumers, but evidence does not establish a concrete regression at the required confidence.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and relevant call paths. Submitted one medium synchronous-ui-work finding for full context-view layout on every frame of the new collapse animation; no boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, eager-work regression, or cleanup leak was found.
